args.text:
The Metropolitan Council of Nashville and Davidson County, down in the southeastern U.S. state of Tennessee, has officially marked fifty years — the 50th anniversary — since the first lot of Kurdish families turned up in the U.S., givin' 'em a big wrap for everythin' they've put into the city's culture, community and economy.

Goin' by an official proclamation VOA got its hands on, the first mob of Kurdish families lobbed in the United States on May 1, 1976. Plenty of 'em ended up settlin' in Nashville, Tennessee, while others set up their own communities in cities and states right across the country.

The proclamation gives a shout-out to how hard the Kurdish community's worked to hang onto its language, culture 'n traditions over the past five decades, while pullin' its weight in Nashville's growth and development.

Accordin' to the document, Nashville's now home to more than 20,000 Kurds, which makes it one of the biggest Kurdish communities in the United States. The city's turned into a proper hub for Kurdish culture and community life.

The proclamation also gives a nod to the long-runnin' ties between the United States and Kurdistan, and to Kurdish Peshmerga forces, U.S. troops and their allies workin' together in the fight against terrorism.

Metropolitan Nashville councillor Mike Cortese, who looks after District 4, got the official recognition of the anniversary up, workin' alongside other councillors.

The proclamation was signed on October 6, 2026.

Talk yourself up; make out you are more important or accomplished than you are.
A mob of (sheep, cattle, roos, people): a herd, flock or crowd.
That lot, that bunch of people or that outfit (I wouldn't trust that mob).
A group of people; a community.
An American (any American, not only a northerner).
A man who moves mobs of cattle or sheep overland over long distances.
